page.layout: One block of verse in one column, left of centre; running head "LYRICA." at top centre; page number "39" at top right; signature "C iiij" at the foot right.

main_text.p:
Possint superā dulcia carpere,
Et te potentem cuncta, Christe,
Supplicibus decorare votis.
Cædes minatur si furor hosticus
Tutum vocatus consilium annuis,
Virésque turbatis fidele
Præsidium, columenque rebus.

Quicunque iusti commoda fœderis
Concessa nobis tristior aspicis,
Quid suspicantem vana curis
Sollicitis animum fatigas?

O, qui duellis præferet ocium
Et læta pacis præmia diliget:
Prodesse cunctis, non nocere,
Incolumes cupimusque paces.

Sed marte si quis nos petat improbo,
Quid magna gentis pectora libera,
Virúsque possit provocata
Perfidus experietur hostis.

Impune fines num populabitur
Nostros, & ignes arcibus ingerei?
Ferroque cum charis nepotes
Coniugibus perimet cruento?

Quo Musa tendis? desine pervicax:
Non hæc suaui convenient Lyræ:
Atque urbe festa fœderatis
Civibus hoc cecinisse carmen.

page.notes: Verse lines are set with ligatures and long-s forms; a few letters in "superā", "Musa", "ingerei", "provocata" and "convenient" are doubtful. Initial letters Q and O are large swash capitals. Plain s used throughout.
